name: Stop Motion
description: The timeline of a stop-motion film of toy-brick scenes: the scene is code in a code editor's scene.js tab, the film plays in Brick Studio, the screen, and scrubs on the timeline, exports as an MP4, and saves to the Drive as one film (its set and its scene). A scene plays sound with sound.at(time, sound, { volume, until }) or actor.sound(time, sound, { volume, until }) to follow an actor across the picture: the sound is any audio file in the Platform named by its URI, charmiq://file/<assetId> (an Asset you upload, download, or generate: create_speech and create_music return assetIds; use 'charmiq://file/' + assetId)

charmiq.command.name: describeFilm
charmiq.command.description: How the film stands. Asked nothing, a summary: the studios and code editors found, whether the scene is staged, the film the scene.js tab makes (its title, seconds, fps, frames, actors, views, its camera's shots from cut to cut and the set each starts on, its set keys, the sounds it plays (each its length and, played once, when it ends) and its figures' footsteps, each walk leaping low parts with the steps it takes before, between and after its leaps and, under three anywhere, the fix, where a camera keeping out of parts was drawn in, and what it logged), and once staged every problem in a line: two actors standing in each other, the camera inside something or its target hidden, an actor appearing or vanishing in the picture within a shot (pop: nobody appears or vanishes in view, so stage it out of view and walk it in, and walk it out of view before hiding it; shown or hidden at a cut, or out of the picture, is no pop), a figure's feet in the set, over nothing, floating, tipped or its body through a part, and a keyed flight short of a part it crosses; counted per kind and ranked the worst first within each. The actor standing at a point the camera aims at, before that point (a jumper passing the bar it aims at), is the shot's own subject, never a problem: counted apart as own. A shot's camera problems of one kind and one cause (the same actor, the same part, or parts of the same component, such as a stand's figures sweeping past) share one line: what stands in the way by its short name, the shot, their span, how many moments and when the worst starts; ask describeFilm with kinds or a span for each moment in full. Or the scene's mistake and its line, and the sounds a scene can play. Asked actors, a span (from, to) or kinds, the full entries of the problems naming any of those actors, over any of that span, of those kinds: overlaps, camera, pops (each actor appearing or vanishing in the picture: its frame and where it stands), footing, clearances (every keyed flight over a part, cleared or not: its least margin, when, and the body's point setting it), leaps (every walk leaping low parts: the steps before, between and after its leaps, and the studs a leap and a step carry it), and close (the actors that come within 2 studs) only when kinds names it

actors.description: Detail the problems, clearances and close actors naming any of these actors (a camera problem names the actor in its way)

from.description: Detail those running at or after this moment (seconds; the film's start when left out)

to.description: Detail those running at or before this moment (seconds; the film's end when left out)

kinds.description: Detail only these: overlap, inside, hidden, own (the camera's own subject before the point it aims at), pop (an actor appearing or vanishing in the picture within a shot), into, above, floating, tipped, through, short (a flight short of its part), clearance (every keyed flight over a part), leaps (every walk leaping low parts) and close (the actors that come within 2 studs, never detailed unless named)

stage.description: none, ambiguous (more than one studio holds a build), staging, staged, left (the person went back to the build) or failed

seconds.description: The scene's length: its own seconds, which every time the film's commands take and give counts in

filmSeconds.description: How long the film runs on the screen, when the scene keys its speed (slow motion runs longer than its seconds, fast motion shorter)

shots.description: The camera's shots: from each cut (or the start) to the next (or the end), seconds, named by its cut

set.description: The build's set standing as it starts, when the scene keys one by then (the build's first set otherwise)

sets.description: Each set.at key: from when (seconds) the build's set it names stands, until the next

extents.description: Each set the film stands on (the one it starts on, then each set keyed), the area its parts stand over in whole studs: its south-west corner (x, z) and size; surfaces() maps it whole. Present only once staged

set.description: The set, when the scene keys it (the build's first set otherwise)

sounds.description: Each sound the scene plays (sound.at, or an actor's .sound to follow it): from when (seconds), the sound (a Platform file's charmiq://file/<assetId> URI, or a shipped sound's name), its own length, its volume (1 as recorded), until when it plays over and over or, played once, when it ends, the actor it follows, and the seconds it fades in from silence and out to silence over. Key a cut or a sound to follow it at its end; listen says where within it its words and its pauses fall

seconds.description: The sound's own length in seconds, as its file decodes; absent when its file cannot be read (listen says why)

ends.description: Played once: the scene's seconds it ends at, its length on from its time at the film's pace. Past the film's seconds, it is cut at the film's end: lengthen the scene or start it earlier

footsteps.description: Each figure whose steps sound (a.footsteps): how many footsteps its laid steps make, from the first (seconds) to the last, and the sounds they take turns at. Laid where it stands on the set, so present once staged

leaps.description: Every walk leaping low parts. Asked nothing: its actor, line, steps before, between and after its leaps, and the fix where it takes fewer than three anywhere (a hurdles race runs three strides between hurdles, and more from the start and to the finish); asked its actor, a span or leaps: each in full, with when each leap sets off and the studs a leap and a step carry it. Laid where it stands on the set, so present once staged
In the detail: when each leap sets off (seconds), one per part leapt

stepsBefore.description: The steps its laid walk takes from its start to its first leap (a start from a crouch wants a run before it)

stepsBetween.description: The steps its laid walk takes between each leap and the next (0: one leap straight after another)

stepsAfter.description: The steps its laid walk takes from its last leap's landing to its end (a finish wants a run through it)

leapStuds.description: In the detail: the studs each leap carries the walker, one per leap; parts spaced a leap's studs and n steps' apart leave n steps between

stepStuds.description: In the detail: the studs a step on its own level carries the walker

fix.description: Where it takes fewer than three steps: the studs to start or end the walk further from its parts, or to space its parts apart

shippedSounds.description: The few sounds Stop Motion ships for its example films, playable by name (sound.at(1, 'engine')). A film's own sounds are files in the Platform, played by URI

shippedSoundsError.description: Why the shipped sounds could not be listed (shippedSounds is then empty): describe the film again to retry

counts.description: Asked nothing, once measured: how many problems of each kind it measured, each moment of a camera line counted, every kind measured named (0 for none): overlap once the stage sized the actors, the rest once staged

own.description: Asked nothing, once staged: how many moments the actor standing at the point the camera aims at stands before that point (a jumper passing the bar it aims at): the shot's own subject, never a problem, so in no count and no line; describeFilm({ kinds: ['own'] }) gives each. Absent for none

problems.description: Asked nothing, once measured: every problem in a line, kind by kind in the order counts names them, the worst first within each kind (the most wrong, then the longest, then the earliest). A shot's camera problems of one kind and one cause share a line (moments counts them), the most time the camera goes wrong first. Ask describeFilm({ actors, from, to, kinds }) for one's full entry, a camera line's every moment

kind.description: overlap (two actors standing in each other), inside (the camera inside a part or an actor), hidden (a part or an actor between the camera and its target), pop (an actor shown or hidden in the picture within a shot), into, above, floating, tipped, through (SEE: footing), or short (a keyed flight not clearing a part it crosses)

actor.description: The figure, for a footing problem or a short flight; pop: the actor shown or hidden

change.description: Pop: appears (shown in the picture where the frame before hid it) or vanishes (hidden where the frame before showed it)

by.description: Inside, hidden: the part (as Brick Studio names it) or the actor; a line of moments, the actor, the part, or the component holding the parts by its name and place (stand-full at x 38 z -15)

shot.description: A line of moments, or a pop: the shot they fall in, when named

from.description: Seconds; a line of moments, from the first to the last; a pop, the first frame showing it (to the same)

moments.description: A line of moments: how many camera problems it holds, each in full in the detail (kinds inside or hidden, or its span)

time.description: A line of moments: when the worst (the longest) starts, seconds. Short: when its margin is least (seconds, the first frame so)

point.description: Short: the body's point lowest over the part then (hips, waist, chest, neck, head, waist front, waist back, chest front, chest back; front is its south at yaw 0): raise the flight there, then

most.description: How much is wrong at most, in unit: an overlap's depth, how far feet go in or stand over, how deep a body goes into a part, how far a flight falls short of its part's top (studs), or how far a figure tilts (degrees). Absent for the camera, whose problem is its span

lines.description: The scene's lines that place the figure's feet then, or the flight's path; pop: the key or path showing or hiding it (or what it rides)

fix.description: Pop: stage it out of view and walk it in (appears), or walk it out of view before hiding it (vanishes)

heldBack.description: Tipped by a key held from outside its walk: a channel's first key lies later than the span and holds back to the film's start (a flight's pitch keyed at its landing lies its walker down from the start), or its last lies before the walk and holds on (a crouch's lean keyed before a race and never keyed back bends the runner the whole race)

keys.description: Each key held: its channel (pitch, roll or lean), its time (seconds) and its scene line

fix.description: The key that holds it upright instead: its channels keyed 0 at the last moment it moves tipped by a key held back (key pitch 0 at 9.125 s), which then holds back to the film's start in their place, or at the first by a key held on (key lean 0 at 26.042 s: the pose's lean), which then holds on in its place

camera.description: Asked for its kinds (inside, hidden, own) or its actors or span: where the camera goes wrong, as spans of seconds, the longest first: standing inside a part of the set or an actor, or one standing between it and its target (an actor riding with the actor it aims at never counts); then where its own subject stands before the point it aims at (own). Present only once staged

kind.description: inside: the camera stands inside it; hidden: it stands between the camera and its target; own: the actor standing at the point the camera aims at (the nearest actor, within its own height of the point, or one riding with it) stands before that point, the shot's own subject and never a blocked picture

by.description: The part (as Brick Studio names it) or the actor

pops.description: Asked for pop or its actors or span: every actor appearing or vanishing in the picture within one shot, in the film's order: hidden in one frame and shown in the next (appears), or shown and then hidden (vanishes), any part of it in frame where it is shown, as screenOf places it. A person sees it pop in or out of nowhere: stage it out of view and walk it in, walk it out of view before hiding it (visible: false). One shown or hidden at a cut, or out of the picture as it changes, is none. Present only once staged

from.description: Seconds: the first frame showing the change

shot.description: The shot it falls in, when named

at.description: Where it stands shown: in the frame it appears in, or the last before it vanishes; x, z (studs) and height (plates)

lines.description: The scene's line of the key or path showing or hiding it (or what it rides): a helper keying visible names the helper's line

footing.description: Asked for its kinds (into, above, floating, tipped, through) or its actors or span: where a figure's feet go wrong, as spans of seconds, kind by kind and the worst first: into, its feet in the set (a walk through a landing or a stair: its path misses the treads, or it climbs more than its step); above, as it steps, its feet out over nothing (walked off a gallery's edge, along at a height with nothing under it, or stood by the ground on a part too narrow for its feet: on names it); floating, as it stands, sits or poses, its lowest point a second or more over what is under it (a sitter keyed over its seat: its height is its seat's top; never while it flies, rising or falling fast as a jump does). Fix the walk's points, its ground (ground(), its step and start) or its keyed height. Also tipped, as it walks or travels along the ground (never lying still), its body more than 45° from upright, its pitch and roll with its lean: lying down or bent over as it walks (key its pitch, roll or pose's lean upright through the walk; a channel's first key holds back to the film's start, so a flight's pitch keyed at its landing lies its walker down from the start, and its last holds on, so a crouch's lean keyed before a race bends its runner the whole race); and through, while it is in the air (more than half a plate over what is under it, or flying), its body in a part of the set: a keyed flight through a bar or a beam (raise or reroute the path). A flight's margin over each part it crosses is in clearances. Present only once staged

kind.description: into, above, floating, tipped or through

most.description: The most its feet reach in or stand over, studs (a plate is 0.4 studs); into shows past 0.3 studs, above past 1.2, floating once it lasts a second; tipped: the most it tilts, degrees; through: how deep its deepest point goes, its least way out of the part (up, down or across)

at.description: Where it stands as the span starts: x, z (studs) and height (plates, its lowest point, counted from the baseplate: never from the surface under it, which surfaceTop gives)

surfaceTop.description: Plates over the baseplate: the top of the part its feet are in (into), or of what is under them (above, floating, tipped); absent over nothing. A figure keyed off the ground is keyed at this height to stand on it

aboveSurface.description: Plates: how far its lowest point stands over surfaceTop (at.height less surfaceTop), below 0 in the part

on.description: Following the ground (ground()): the part the ground stands it on, whose top is the level it walks at, named as camera problems name one: a bar or a ledge it stepped up onto within its step (lower the step, or walk round it)

part.description: Through: the part, named as camera problems name one

points.description: Through: the body's points in the part when it goes deepest (hips, waist, chest, neck, head, waist front, waist back, chest front, chest back; front is its south at yaw 0)

by.description: What places its feet as the span starts: walk (a walk holds the level it starts on unless the actor follows the ground), path (a path keying its height), or keys (its height keys: a key's value eases in from the key before over the whole time between them, so a figure keyed 0 now and 6 plates ten seconds on rises the whole ten seconds; key the later one 'hold' to keep the earlier value until it)

lines.description: The scene's lines that place its feet then: the walk's, the path's, or the height keys it eases between

keys.description: The height keys easing then, each its time (seconds) and height (plates); one when it holds the last. By walk (off the ground), those easing as the walk starts: a walk holds the height its keys give it as it starts, whatever they key later

tilts.description: Tipped by keys: the pitch, roll or lean keys tipping it then, each its time (seconds), channel and value (degrees)

heldBack.description: Tipped by a key held from outside its walk: a channel's first key lies later than the span and holds back to the film's start (a flight's pitch keyed at its landing lies its walker down from the start), or its last lies before the walk and holds on (a crouch's lean keyed before a race and never keyed back bends the runner the whole race)

keys.description: Each key held: its channel (pitch, roll or lean), its time (seconds) and its scene line

fix.description: The key that holds it upright instead: its channels keyed 0 at the last moment it moves tipped by a key held back (key pitch 0 at 9.125 s), which then holds back to the film's start in their place, or at the first by a key held on (key lean 0 at 26.042 s: the pose's lean), which then holds on in its place

clearances.description: Asked for clearance or short, or its actors or span: each keyed flight (a path keying a figure's height) over each part it crosses whose top rises above both the surface under its takeoff and the one under its landing, the least margin first. A fact, cleared or not, so a fix reads its margin before and after; one not cleared is also a problem (short). Present only once staged

from.description: Seconds: the first moment its body is over the part

part.description: The part, named as camera problems name one

margin.description: Studs: the least its body clears the part's top by; below 0 it passes through it (-0.36 means raise the flight 0.36 studs, 0.9 plates, or move the part)

time.description: Seconds: when the margin is least (the first frame so), on the way up, at the top or on the way down

point.description: The body's point setting the margin then (hips, waist, chest, neck, head, waist front, waist back, chest front, chest back; front is its south at yaw 0): a pitched body's lowest point, which a fix raises at that moment. The body alone is measured, never what its hands hold

cleared.description: Whether the margin is 0 or more

lines.description: The scene's line of the flight's path

avoided.description: Where a camera keyed avoid: 'parts' was drawn in toward its target to keep clear of the set's parts, as spans of seconds, each with the least share of its keyed distance it kept and the view it is (absent for the film's camera)

overlaps.description: Asked for overlap or its actors or span: every two actors standing in each other (more than half a stud, by their boxes), as spans of seconds, the deepest first, with the most they stand in, studs: people walking through people, or parked on one spot. A figure's box is about 3 studs across its arms and 2 deep, so two side by side stand 4 studs apart. Fix: keep their walks apart in place or time, park each on a spot of its own, or walk one out of view and hide it (visible: false) once its part is over; a thing in a figure's hand is its hand's (rightHand: { part, color }), never an actor beside it, and a thing thrown is an actor shown from its release. Present only once staged

time.description: The first moment they stand the most in each other

positions.description: Where each stands then, by name: x, z (studs) and height (plates)

close.description: Only when kinds names close: the actors that come near each other, candidates to look at for a possible collision, never problems themselves. Present only once staged: stage the film when it is absent

withinStuds.description: The gap between two actors' boxes, studs, under which they count as close

pairs.description: Every two actors that come within withinStuds while both are shown, each where they come closest, the nearest first. Two riding together never count, nor an actor while hidden; a thing shown from its release beside its thrower counts as any other actor

file.description: The film's file in the Drive: its name once saved or opened, and whether the set or the scene changed since (a film never saved has changed)

charmiq.command.name: motionOf
charmiq.command.description: One actor's motion over a span, to see what a still cannot: its place (x, z studs; height plates, counted from the baseplate: never from the surface under it) and turn (yaw, pitch, roll degrees) at evenly spaced samples, following the ground (ground()) the surface's top the ground stands it on (ground, plates from the baseplate), from which its keys and paths count (height less ground is what they give it: a flop's path counts from the bar's top while its footprint overlaps the bar), and for each of those values what drives it over the span (its walk, a path, its keys, or nothing) with the scene lines that do, a key read before it named as holding its value back. Read it after a note or a footing problem names an actor, to find the line to change

to.description: Seconds (the film's end when left out)

ground.description: Following the ground: the top (plates from the baseplate) of the surface the ground stands it on, from which its keys and paths count; key height less ground to place it

by.description: walk (its walk lays it), path (a path keys it), keys (its keys), or none

heldBack.description: Read before this channel's first key: that key's value is held back from its time (seconds) to the film's start. A figure whose only pitch key is at its landing lies at that pitch all through its run-up: key the value it should have earlier

by.description: walk (its walk lays it), path (a path keys it), keys (its keys), or none

heldBack.description: Read before this channel's first key: that key's value is held back from its time (seconds) to the film's start. A figure whose only pitch key is at its landing lies at that pitch all through its run-up: key the value it should have earlier

by.description: walk (its walk lays it), path (a path keys it), keys (its keys), or none

heldBack.description: Read before this channel's first key: that key's value is held back from its time (seconds) to the film's start. A figure whose only pitch key is at its landing lies at that pitch all through its run-up: key the value it should have earlier

by.description: walk (its walk lays it), path (a path keys it), keys (its keys), or none

heldBack.description: Read before this channel's first key: that key's value is held back from its time (seconds) to the film's start. A figure whose only pitch key is at its landing lies at that pitch all through its run-up: key the value it should have earlier

by.description: walk (its walk lays it), path (a path keys it), keys (its keys), or none

heldBack.description: Read before this channel's first key: that key's value is held back from its time (seconds) to the film's start. A figure whose only pitch key is at its landing lies at that pitch all through its run-up: key the value it should have earlier

by.description: walk (its walk lays it), path (a path keys it), keys (its keys), or none

heldBack.description: Read before this channel's first key: that key's value is held back from its time (seconds) to the film's start. A figure whose only pitch key is at its landing lies at that pitch all through its run-up: key the value it should have earlier

charmiq.command.name: where
charmiq.command.description: Where every actor shown stands at a moment, by time (seconds) or frame (from 0), the playhead's frame when neither is given, and how it is turned (yaw clockwise seen from above, degrees), and where the film's camera stands and looks: x east and z north in studs, height in plates

current.description: Present when no time or frame was given: the frame is the one the film's playhead stands on

set.description: The build's set standing, when the scene keys one by then (the build's first set otherwise)

target.description: The point it aims at. An actor it looks at is followed as a camera operator follows one, so the point can stand off the actor: its height and its place over about a second (a leap or a hop moves nothing; a climb still tilts, a run still pans); its exact place where the key says lock: true

charmiq.command.name: measure
charmiq.command.description: Where two actors come closest over the film (or from and to, seconds): the frame, the gap between their boxes in studs (each box its footprint turned by its yaw and its height, unposed; 0 when they touch) and where each stood

positions.description: Each actor's position then: x east and z north in studs, height in plates

charmiq.command.name: listen
charmiq.command.description: Hear a sound you cannot hear: any a scene can play (a Platform file's charmiq://file/<assetId> URI, or a shipped sound's name). Answers its length and the spans it sounds over, first to last, parted by its pauses: each span from and to in seconds, and the pause after it. A pause is at least minPause seconds (0.3 when left out) more than 40 dB quieter than the sound's loudest, its loudness heard in 20 ms windows, so a whisper still sounds. To sync a film to narration, listen to it, map its sentences onto the spans in order (a line's commas and breaths may part it into more than one; the pauses its text marks fall at span ends), and key cuts, actions and effects to the spans' times. At most 60 spans: a sound with more is parted only at its 59 longest pauses, and capped says how many it held. Refuses a sound no scene can play, or one that cannot be read or decoded, saying why

sound.description: The sound: a Platform file's charmiq://file/<assetId> URI, or a shipped sound's name (describeFilm shippedSounds)

minPause.description: The shortest pause in seconds that parts two spans, 0.05 to 10 (0.3 when left out): longer joins a sentence's phrases, shorter parts its words
The shortest pause in seconds that parted the spans

spans.description: Where the sound sounds, first to last; none for a silence

pause.description: The seconds of silence after it, before the next span; absent on the last

capped.description: Present when the sound held more than 60 spans: how many it held. The spans then part at its 59 longest pauses alone

charmiq.command.name: surfaces
charmiq.command.description: What stands where on the set, as a map: a row a z, north at the top, each row's cells west to east as runs of like cells, each run its first cell's x and its tops (-25:b2x8b@6 -22:b2x8b@6/p1x10o@14 -21:b2x8b@6: a mat from x -25, the bar over it in the column at x -22 alone, the mat again from x -21 to the row's east), each top lowest first its part's key, @ and its height in plates (b2x8b@6/p1x10o@14: a mat's top at 6 plates and a bar's at 14 over it), 0 alone the bare baseplate, a dash for none. A key is read off its part's name, its kind then its color (brick-2x8 blue b2x8b, plate-1x10 orange p1x10o), so a part has the same key in every ask; the legend names each (two parts of one map whose names key alike take their whole names, brick-2x4.blue). Asked no area, the whole set: its extent and a map of it a cell of several studs a side when it is larger than 64 by 64 (cell, each run's x its first cell's west stud), each cell the tops most of its studs show (the higher of as many); then ask an area of it for every stud. Read it to see where a track, a lane, a mat or a bar stands before routing a walk or a flight there, or after a note says something is off its place. The film staged

x.description: The area's west cell, studs (all four left out: the whole set)

width.description: Cells east (at most 64 by 64 cells in all)

time.description: The moment whose set is read (0 when left out): the build's set standing then

set.description: The set read, when the scene keys one by then (the build's first set otherwise)

extent.description: Asked no area: the area the set's parts stand over, whole studs (absent, with no rows, for a set without parts)

cell.description: Asked no area: the studs a side of each cell, the least that fits the whole set within 64 by 64 cells

west.description: The x of each row's first cell (its west stud)

east.description: The x of each row's last cell (its west stud)

cells.description: Its cells west to east as runs of like cells, a space between: each x:tops, x the run's first cell's west stud, the run reaching to the next run's x (the row's east for the last)

legend.description: Each key the cells use, the part it names by its kind and color (t2x4o: tile-2x4 orange): every top of that part and color, wherever it stands, under the same key in every ask

charmiq.command.name: stage
charmiq.command.description: Stage the scene's film again on the studios: casts its actors from the build and shows them, after the build changed or the person went back to it. Answers how the stage then stands; describeFilm then says what is wrong

stage.description: none, ambiguous (more than one studio holds a build), staged, left (the person went back to the build) or failed

charmiq.command.name: seek
charmiq.command.description: Show one moment of the film in the studios, by time (seconds) or frame (from 0); resolves once the studio has drawn it, so a screenshot next sees it

time.description: The scene's seconds from the start (the frame showing that moment, however the scene's speed stretches it)

charmiq.command.name: storyboard
charmiq.command.description: Show a storyboard of the film on the Brick Studio holding the build: up to 12 of its frames at once, each captioned with its time, frame and shot, through a view when named (a plan view shows each moment from above, with every actor's path and the camera). Resolves once the sheet shows; take an Application screenshot of that Brick Studio to read it. The sheet closes when the film next moves. Give times, frames or a shot, one of them: a shot shows 4 of its frames, its first, two between at a third and two thirds of the way, and its last, so one screenshot shows the shot's motion where a seek and a screenshot show one moment. Left without any, it shows the middle of each shot

shot.description: A shot's name, as describeFilm's shots name it: its first frame, two between and its last (each frame of a shot shorter than 4)

view.description: One of the scene's views (the film's camera when left out)

charmiq.command.name: screenOf
charmiq.command.description: Where every actor stands on the screen at a moment, by time (seconds) or frame (from 0), as the main studio's camera draws it, and the camera's problem then, if any (describeFilm camera). Read the film as it looks without a screenshot: whether an actor is in frame, how much of the frame it fills, which side it stands on. Once the film is staged

actors.description: Each actor the studio cast and the frame shows, by name

additionalProperties.description: Its box on the screen: left, top, right and bottom as shares of the frame (0 to 1 across and down, past them where it runs off), its middle, how far ahead its nearest corner stands (studs) and whether any of it is in frame; only behind: true when it stands wholly behind the camera

kind.description: inside: the camera stands inside it; hidden: it stands between the camera and its target; own: the actor standing at the point the camera aims at (the nearest actor, within its own height of the point, or one riding with it) stands before that point, the shot's own subject and never a blocked picture

by.description: The part (as Brick Studio names it) or the actor

charmiq.command.name: reviewCuts
charmiq.command.description: Every cut of the film read as an editor reads it: the last frame of the shot before and the first after, each side's subject, where it stands on the screen and which way it moves, how far the camera turns (degrees), how long each shot runs, and what an editor would flag: a subject crossing the line (moving one way before the cut and the other after), jumping across the screen, a cut turning the camera under 30 degrees on one subject, a shot under a second, a subject out of frame, the camera inside something or its target hidden. A shot no frame shows is passed over. Once the film is staged

frame.description: The first frame after the cut

subject.description: The actor the camera aims at, else the one filling most of the frame

screen.description: Its box on the screen: left, top, right and bottom as shares of the frame (0 to 1 across and down, past them where it runs off), its middle, how far ahead its nearest corner stands (studs) and whether any of it is in frame; only behind: true when it stands wholly behind the camera

moving.description: Which way the subject moves across the frame over its shot's few frames that side, as this frame's camera sees it (left, right, up, down or still); absent for a shot of one frame

subject.description: The actor the camera aims at, else the one filling most of the frame

screen.description: Its box on the screen: left, top, right and bottom as shares of the frame (0 to 1 across and down, past them where it runs off), its middle, how far ahead its nearest corner stands (studs) and whether any of it is in frame; only behind: true when it stands wholly behind the camera

moving.description: Which way the subject moves across the frame over its shot's few frames that side, as this frame's camera sees it (left, right, up, down or still); absent for a shot of one frame

charmiq.command.name: listFilms
charmiq.command.description: The films (and designs) in the films folder of the Drive, each by name and uri

charmiq.command.name: saveFilm
charmiq.command.description: Save the film (the main Brick Studio's build, the set, and the scene.js tab's scene) as one film in the Drive: under name in the films folder, or over its own file (the one it was opened from or saved as, wherever it is) when it has one. A name other than its own file's saves a new file, the film's own from then on, and leaves the earlier one as it was: name a film run again to keep the one before. Another film of that name is refused unless replace is true

folder.description: The folder saved to, when known

charmiq.command.name: openFilm
charmiq.command.description: Open a film from the Drive (its uri from listFilms, or its name): its set into the main Brick Studio's build and its scene into the scene.js tab. A plain design opens its set alone, the scene kept. Refused while the film has unsaved changes (the document never saved it, or it has changes since it was saved) unless discard is true

discard.description: Go on without saving the film's unsaved changes

scene.description: Whether the file carried a scene

charmiq.command.name: newFilm
charmiq.command.description: Start a new film: the main Brick Studio's build cleared (its ground kept) and a starter scene in the scene.js tab. Refused while the film has unsaved changes (the document never saved it, or it has changes since it was saved) unless discard is true; save the film first to keep it

discard.description: Go on without saving the film's unsaved changes
